summary: Vanuatu has sold citizenship under several schemes: 1990s passport sales, the Capital Investment Immigration Plan (CIIP, from 2014), the post-Cyclone Pam VERP honorary citizenship (2015 to March 2017), the Development Support Program (DSP) and Contribution Program (VCP) since 2017, and a Real Estate Option Program (2021); a 2011-2015 Hong Kong residence-visa scheme is included as a residence programme. Legal texts and fee orders come from the Citizenship Office website; revenue comes from Treasury monthly and half-year reports, agency revenue reports (which split DSP/VCP and CIIP receipts) and IMF Article IV tables, giving an annual revenue series for 2015-2025 and half-year 2026. Official counts of applications, approvals or passports by year were not found; the only counts are EU-cited figures already in the dataset and Guardian reporting.

programs.name: Vanuatu investor citizenship schemes (all schemes; the IMF's "Economic Citizenship Program", ECP)
programs.notes: Umbrella id for figures that cover several schemes at once. Government accounts book VDSP and VCP receipts together as "Honorary Citizenship Program Fees" and, from 2024, report them together with the CIIP. Schemes over time: 1990s passport sales; CIIP (2014-); VERP honorary citizenship (2015-March 2017); VDSP and VCP (2017-); REO (2021-). Run by the Citizenship Office and Commission; due diligence by the Financial Intelligence Unit. Citizenship is granted without residence; Part 3A of the Citizenship Act allows dual citizenship.

programs.name: Capital Investment Immigration Plan (CIIP)
programs.notes: Citizenship for investors (Form D), legal basis s.13B-13C of the Citizenship Act inserted by Act No. 39 of 2013 (in force 21 Jan 2014), linked to a residence permit under the Immigration Visa Regulation No. 180 of 2011. IMF (2015): USD 260,000 investment returnable after 7 years (25% NBV deposit, 25% government bonds, 50% real investment) plus a $40,000 fee. The Citizenship Office now lists a "Citizenship Fee" of USD 260,000 for applicant, spouse and one child. Practically dormant in 2020 (VT 10,000 receipts), reactivated as a cheaper alternative in 2024, suspended March 2025 and resumed June 2025 (IMF).

programs.name: Vanuatu Economic Rehabilitation Program (VERP), honorary citizenship after Cyclone Pam
programs.notes: Honorary citizenship sold to raise revenue after Cyclone Pam (March 2015), using the honorary citizenship power in s.20 of the Citizenship Act. ABC reported a launch in Hong Kong in April 2015 (price $162,000, quota 100); the IMF dates the launch to late 2015. Phased out by March 2017 and replaced by the VDSP and VCP (Treasury).

programs.name: Vanuatu Development Support Program (DSP / VDSP)
programs.notes: Main scheme since 2017; first run as "Honorary Citizenship DSP" (fees reduced by Order No. 94 of 2018), put on a statutory footing by s.13E (Act No. 34 of 2018, in force 7 Jan 2019) and regulated by Order No. 33 of 2019 (24 Apr 2019): government fee USD 80,000 (single) to 130,000 (couple and two children), minimum selling price via licensed Vanuatu-citizen agents USD 130,000 to 180,000, FIU due diligence (USD 2,000, USD 5,000 from 27 Mar 2020). Decision within 3 months; no residence required.

programs.name: Vanuatu Contribution Program (VCP)
programs.notes: Legal basis s.13D of the Citizenship Act and the Citizenship (Contribution Program) Regulations Order No. 220 of 2016 (not found online); amended by Order No. 34 of 2019 and Order No. 38 of 2020. Same government minimum contribution and minimum selling price as the DSP (Citizenship Office directive, April 2020). Launch date taken from the Treasury statement that VDSP and VCP replaced VERP by March 2017. Industry sources say it was reserved for Chinese applicants; not confirmed officially.

programs.name: Real Estate Option Program (REO)
programs.notes: Citizenship for buying property in a Vanuatu Government Approved Project plus prescribed fees; s.13F of the Citizenship Act and Regulation Order No. 93 of 2021; sole master agent Naika Holdings Ltd. An earlier REO route (s.13CA, Act No. 18 of 2014, in force 8 Jul 2014) was repealed by Act No. 40 of 2014 (23 Jan 2015). The Treasury said in 2021-22 its revenue potential was low or unproven. Prices not found.

programs.name: Hong Kong Permanent Residency (HKPR) Visa Program
programs.notes: Residence (not citizenship) for mainland Chinese investors seeking Hong Kong permanent residency via Hong Kong's Capital Investment Entrant Scheme: investment of at least 300,000 vatu in a Vanuatu company through a Hong Kong agent, 10-year visa. About 1,500 investors; suspended after Hong Kong suspended its scheme in January 2015 (IMF). No path to citizenship stated.

programs.name: 1990s passport-sale schemes
programs.notes: The IMF (2015) describes attempts in the 1990s to sell passports, about 300 passports sold in 1996-1997, and reports of illegal issuance that led some countries, such as Canada, to drop visa waivers. Names, legal basis and dates not found in official sources.

gaps: No official annual statistics on applications, approvals, rejections or passports issued under any scheme; the Citizenship Office publishes no annual report online. Counts exist only via the EU (already in the dataset) and the Guardian (2020).

Principal regulations not found: Citizenship (Contribution Program) Regulations Order No. 220 of 2016, Order No. 34 of 2019 (VCP), Order No. 94 of 2018 (DSP fee reduction), the VERP/honorary citizenship order, the CIIP regulations (Immigration Visa Regulation No. 180 of 2011 and later orders) and the REO Regulation Order No. 93 of 2021, so REO prices and the original VCP/VERP prices are missing.

2026 changes reported by industry sites (Citizenship (Development Support Programme) Regulations (Amendment) Order No. 39 of 2026 and Contribution Programme Order No. 40 of 2026, Gazette No. 25 of 2026, 19 March 2026) could not be confirmed in an official source.
PacLII (paclii.org), which holds Vanuatu gazettes and subsidiary legislation, refused automated downloads (HTTP 403).

No audited figures: all Vanuatu revenue figures are unaudited Treasury/agency figures (status provisional). Different government documents give different totals for the same year (e.g. 2022: VT 8,483.1m vs 7,663.2m; 2023: VT 8,115.0m vs 8,399.1m; 2025 budget VT 7,629.5m vs 7,729.7m), with no explanation.

No breakdown of revenue by nationality or by scheme before 2020; CIIP receipts are only separated in the 2020, 2023 and H1 2024 agency revenue reports. 2018 and 2024 full-year agency revenue reports not found.
